newsitem.title: USA: Nevada senators clear way for nuclear waste debate.
newsitem.headline: Nevada senators clear way for nuclear waste debate.

text.p: Nevada's senators Tuesday cleared the way for the Senate to begin debate on a bill that would make the government build a temporary facility in Nevada to store nuclear waste, said an aide to Senator Richard Bryan.
Debate on the controversial bill, which the Clinton administration has said it would veto in its current form, is scheduled to begin at 1300 EDT/1700 GMT Wednesday.

The two Nevada Democrats, Bryan and Senator Harry Reid, who have bitterly fought having spent fuel from nuclear power plants dumped in their state, had aimed to prolong debate indefinitely on whether to let the bill come to the floor.

A vote to cut off the filibuster was scheduled for Tuesday afternoon but was cancelled when the Nevadans saw they were going to lose the vote, and agreed to let the bill come to the floor, said Bryan's spokeswoman Karen Kirchgasser.
"There didn't seem to be much point in going through with it," Kirchgasser said.
Bryan and Reid are keeping their options open on whether to try to slow down debate and block a vote on the bill itself once it comes to the floor, she said.

The bill, pushed by nuclear utilities, would require the government to build temporary storage for 30,000 tons of spent fuel from nuclear plants by the end of 1999, to be used until the government constructs a permanent dump.

The issue of temporary storage must be resolved this year because by law, the government is required to start taking responsibility for spent fuel from power plants by February 1998, but it has nowhere to put the nuclear waste yet.

Nevada's Yucca Mountain is the only site the Energy Department is investigating as a potential permanent dump for spent nuclear fuel. It expects to decide in the fall of 1998 whether the site would be safe for burying the waste.

The legislation by Republican Sen. Frank Murkowski of Alaska and Larry Craig of Idaho calls for the Energy Department to build the storage facility at the government's Nevada Test Site near Yucca Mountain, or at another site if the mountain is determined to be unsafe for a permanent dump.
The Clinton administration does not want to be forced into shipping nuclear waste to Nevada before it knows that the spent fuel could safely be buried in Yucca Mountain in the long run.
